headline.en: Three scientists. Three realms — sky, earth, and life.
headline.zh: 三个科学家，三个领域 — 天空、大地、生命。

subtext.en: Which one pulled you in first when you looked up as a kid?
subtext.zh: 小时候抬头看世界，最先把你拉进去的是哪一个？

definition.en: A scientist who studies the heavens — stars, planets, galaxies, and the laws that govern them.
definition.zh: 研究天空的科学家 — 恒星、行星、星系，以及支配它们的规律。

etymology.en: From Greek astron = 'star' + nomos = 'law, arrangement'. Literally: 'one who measures the laws of stars.'
etymology.zh: 希腊词根 astron = 星 + nomos = 规律、安排。字面意思：丈量星辰规律的人。

sentences.en: The astronomer spent twelve years verifying a single dataset — patience is half the job.
sentences.zh: 天文学家花了十二年核实一组数据 — 耐心是这份工作的一半。

sentences.en: An astronomer tells children: the star you're pointing at may have stopped burning before you were born.
sentences.zh: 天文学家会告诉孩子：你指着的那颗星，可能在你出生前就已经熄灭了。

mnemonic.en: Astron = STAR. The astronomer reads light that's been traveling longer than any of us has been alive.
mnemonic.zh: Astron = 星。天文学家读的是光 — 它已经赶了比我们任何人都长的路。

question.en: An astronomer and an astrologer share the same root. What's the difference?
question.zh: 天文学家和占星师共用同一个词根。区别在哪里？

answer.en: The astronomer measures the stars. The astrologer reads them like a horoscope. One is science, one is storytelling.
answer.zh: 天文学家在丈量星辰。占星师把星辰读成命运。一个是科学，一个是讲故事。

anecdote.en: Vera Rubin spent decades counting starlight in distant galaxies and found something nobody could explain — galaxies were spinning too fast. Her quiet measurements gave us the idea of 'dark matter.' One astronomer, patient enough to trust her numbers.
anecdote.zh: 薇拉·鲁宾用几十年数遥远星系的星光，发现一件没人能解释的事 — 星系转得太快了。她安静的测量给了我们'暗物质'这个概念。一个天文学家，愿意相信自己的数字到底。

definition.en: A scientist who studies the earth itself — its rocks, layers, minerals, and the deep history pressed into them.
definition.zh: 研究地球本身的科学家 — 岩石、地层、矿物，以及压在其中的深远历史。

etymology.en: From Greek ge = 'earth' + logos = 'study'. Literally: 'the study of the earth.'
etymology.zh: 希腊词根 ge = 大地 + logos = 学问。字面意思：研究大地的学问。

sentences.en: The geologist looked at the cliff face for an hour and read it like a book — every band a chapter.
sentences.zh: 地质学家盯着悬崖看了一个小时，像读书一样把它读完了 — 每一层颜色都是一章。

sentences.en: Every pebble in your hand was once part of a mountain — that's the first sentence a geologist learns.
sentences.zh: 你手心里的每一颗石子，曾经都是一座山的一部分 — 这是地质学家学到的第一句话。

mnemonic.en: Ge = EARTH. The geologist reads rock the way you'd read a diary the planet kept for itself.
mnemonic.zh: Ge = 大地。地质学家读岩石的方式，就像在读地球给自己写的日记。

question.en: A geographer and a geologist both study the earth. What's the difference?
question.zh: 地理学家和地质学家都研究地球。区别在哪里？

answer.en: The geographer studies the SURFACE — rivers, cities, climate. The geologist studies what's UNDERNEATH — layers, time, deep structure.
answer.zh: 地理学家研究表面 — 河流、城市、气候。地质学家研究底下 — 地层、时间、深层结构。

anecdote.en: When the Grand Canyon was first measured, geologists realized its bottom layers were two billion years old — older than most multicellular life. Visitors came to see scenery. The geologists were looking at time.
anecdote.zh: 当大峡谷第一次被测量时，地质学家意识到它最底层的岩石有二十亿年 — 比大多数多细胞生命都古老。游客来看风景，地质学家来看的是时间。

definition.en: A scientist who studies living things — from a single cell to a whole forest — and the rules that life follows.
definition.zh: 研究生命的科学家 — 从一个细胞到一整片森林，以及生命遵循的规律。

etymology.en: From Greek bios = 'life' + logos = 'study'. Literally: 'the study of life.'
etymology.zh: 希腊词根 bios = 生命 + logos = 学问。字面意思：研究生命的学问。

sentences.en: A biologist watches one tide pool for a year and learns more than most labs learn in a decade.
sentences.zh: 生物学家盯一个潮池盯一年，学到的，比许多实验室十年还多。

sentences.en: Every biologist's favorite line: life finds a way — and it does, again and again.
sentences.zh: 每个生物学家最喜欢的一句话：生命总会找到出路 — 而且它真的会，一次又一次。

mnemonic.en: Bios = LIFE. From the bacteria on your skin to the whales in the deep — every living thing is the biologist's office.
mnemonic.zh: Bios = 生命。从你皮肤上的细菌到深海的鲸鱼 — 每一个活物都是生物学家的办公室。

question.en: A biologist studies LIFE. So what's the difference between a biologist and a zoologist or botanist?
question.zh: 生物学家研究生命。那他和动物学家、植物学家的区别在哪里？

answer.en: Biologist is the umbrella. Zoologists focus on animals, botanists on plants — both are biologists who picked one corner of the kingdom.
answer.zh: 生物学家是大伞。动物学家专攻动物，植物学家专攻植物 — 他们都是生物学家，只是各选了王国的一角。

anecdote.en: Rachel Carson was a biologist before she was an author. She listened carefully to what was disappearing from American springs — birds, frogs, insects — and wrote 'Silent Spring.' One biologist who could hear what was missing changed environmental law forever.
anecdote.zh: 蕾切尔·卡逊先是生物学家，才成为作家。她仔细倾听美国的春天里在消失的东西 — 鸟、青蛙、虫子 — 然后写了《寂静的春天》。一个能听见缺席之声的生物学家，永远改变了环境法律。

setup.en: Both look at things older than you. Both treat time as the most interesting ingredient.
setup.zh: 他们看的都是比你古老的东西。时间，是他们眼里最有意思的成分。

leftLine.en: Looks up. Reads light from millions of years ago.
leftLine.zh: 抬头看。读的是几百万年前出发的光。

leftMnemonic.en: Astron = STAR · time, written in light.
leftMnemonic.zh: Astron = 星 · 时间，用光写成。

rightLine.en: Looks down. Reads rock pressed into layers.
rightLine.zh: 低头看。读的是被压成层的岩石。

rightMnemonic.en: Ge = EARTH · time, written in stone.
rightMnemonic.zh: Ge = 大地 · 时间，用石头写成。

closing.en: One reads light. One reads stone. Both are reading the past.
closing.zh: 一个读光，一个读石。读的都是过去。

reflection.en: Whichever direction you look — up, down, or at your own breath — you're looking at time. The trick is to notice you're inside it too.
reflection.zh: 无论你看哪个方向 — 抬头、低头、还是看自己的呼吸 — 你看的都是时间。关键是意识到，自己也在它里面。

gloss.en: Literally 'a sailor of the stars' — astron (star) + nautes (sailor, as in 'nautical').
gloss.zh: 字面是'星之航行者' — astron（星）+ nautes（水手，同'航海的'）。

usage.en: Every astronaut says the same thing on returning: the earth looks small, and unreasonably beautiful.
usage.zh: 每个宇航员回来都说同一句话：地球看上去很小，又美得不讲道理。

gloss.en: The art of reading meaning into the stars — astron (star) + logos (here meaning 'discourse, talk').
gloss.zh: 把意义读进星辰的技艺 — astron（星）+ logos（此处指'谈论、解读'）。

usage.en: Astrology will never predict the weather, but it predicts what someone wants to believe about themselves.
usage.zh: 占星术从来预测不了天气，但它能预测一个人想怎么相信自己。

gloss.en: Literally 'a bad star' — dis- (negative) + astron. The ancients believed catastrophes came from unlucky alignments.
gloss.zh: 字面是'坏的星' — dis-（负向）+ astron。古人相信厄运来自星辰错位。

usage.en: Real disasters are rarely sudden — they're slow accumulations someone decided to ignore.
usage.zh: 真正的灾难很少是突然的 — 大多是有人选择忽略的缓慢累积。

gloss.en: Literally 'a little star' — astron + -isk (Greek diminutive). The * symbol we use as a footnote mark.
gloss.zh: 字面是'小星星' — astron + -isk（希腊小词后缀）。也就是我们做脚注的 * 符号。

usage.en: His promise came with three asterisks and a footnote — read the fine print.
usage.zh: 他的承诺带着三个星号和一行小注 — 务必读那些小字。

gloss.en: Literally 'writing the earth' — ge (earth) + graphein (to write). The study of places and how they sit together.
gloss.zh: 字面是'写大地' — ge（大地）+ graphein（写）。研究地方与它们之间如何相邻。

usage.en: Geography decides more of your life than you'd like — where you're born sets half your options.
usage.zh: 地理决定的事比你愿意承认的要多 — 你生在哪里，已经定下了一半的可能。

gloss.en: Literally 'measuring the earth' — ge (earth) + metron (measure). Began as a tool to survey flooded fields.
gloss.zh: 字面是'丈量大地' — ge（大地）+ metron（量）。最初是为了在洪水退后重新丈量农田。

usage.en: The Egyptians invented geometry because the Nile kept erasing their fences.
usage.zh: 埃及人发明几何，是因为尼罗河老把他们的田埂冲掉。

gloss.en: Relating to heat from inside the earth — ge (earth) + therme (heat). Same therme as 'thermometer.'
gloss.zh: 与地球内部热量有关 — ge（大地）+ therme（热）。'温度计'里的同一个 therme。

usage.en: Iceland heats most of its homes with geothermal water — the planet does the work for free.
usage.zh: 冰岛大部分的家庭供暖靠地热水 — 地球替他们免费干活。

gloss.en: Literally 'writing a life' — bios (life) + graphein (to write).
gloss.zh: 字面是'写一个人的生命' — bios（生命）+ graphein（写）。

usage.en: A good biography doesn't just list events — it shows you the years between them.
usage.zh: 好的传记不只列出事件 — 它让你看见事件之间的那些年。

gloss.en: Literally 'against life' — anti- (against) + bios. A drug that kills bacterial life inside you.
gloss.zh: 字面是'对抗生命' — anti-（对抗）+ bios。杀死你体内细菌生命的药。

usage.en: Antibiotics changed medicine in twenty years — and we're already using them up.
usage.zh: 抗生素在二十年里改变了医学 — 而我们已经在把它用尽。

gloss.en: Literally 'living together' — syn- (together) + bios. Two species relying on each other.
gloss.zh: 字面是'一起生活' — syn-（一起）+ bios。两个物种相互依赖。

usage.en: The best long-term relationships are quiet symbiosis — each person better off because the other is there.
usage.zh: 最好的长久关系是安静的共生 — 因为对方在，每个人都活得更好一点。

gloss.en: Literally 'household law' — oikos (house) + nomos (law). Same nomos that 'astronomer' uses for the laws of stars.
gloss.zh: 字面是'家庭的规律' — oikos（家）+ nomos（规律）。和'天文学家'里管星辰的 nomos 是同一个。

usage.en: An economy is just millions of tiny household decisions, added up and pretending to be a single thing.
usage.zh: 经济不过是几百万个家庭的小决定，加在一起，假装成一个整体。

gloss.en: Literally 'self-law' — autos (self) + nomos (law). The freedom to make your own rules.
gloss.zh: 字面是'自己的规律' — autos（自己）+ nomos（规律）。给自己定规则的自由。

usage.en: Real autonomy isn't doing what you want — it's knowing why you wanted it.
usage.zh: 真正的自主，不是想做什么就做什么 — 是知道自己为什么想做。
